doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Musicians versus accountants running record companies
summary: Conniff says Miller and Goddard Lieberson were musicians while today's companies are run by accountants, and he thanks DJs, the press and fans.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Great. Well I wish you a lot of success with it and I am fascinated by your combination over the years of business sense, with the great musicianship. That’s rare. I think that’s rare. Because I’ve talked to a number of people who bemoan the fact that the people in power in the music world these days seem to have no musical sense or whatever. And so it’s nice to see it.

Well there has been quite a change. When I started I mentioned Mitch Miller who was an oboe player, and Goddard Lieberson who was president of Columbia Records was a graduate of Juilliard. And they were musicians, or if they weren’t musicians they were guys that wished they could have been musicians that were in [coughs] they were musicians or guys that at least wished they could have been musicians. Now in the record companies they are more concentrating on what’s at the bottom line, how much money did we make or lose, and they have accountants and attorneys running the companies. And I liked it better when the musicians were running the companies. I owe a lot to the fellows that gave me my chance you know, to do that, and I owe a lot to disc jockeys too, they played the heck out of my stuff in the beginning, and fellows like you that did interviews and wrote articles on my music too, and in the trade magazine Down

Beat and Record World and Variety and those magazines, Billboard. They really gave me a lot of space. Of course in the final analysis I had owe a lot to the people that I hit that heart string and recorded that song they fell in love to, and they went out and bought the albums. I have to thank all them too. They’ve been great and they’ve stayed with me for years.
